position_sizing.conditional_logic: Lot = max(0.1, round(Balance/50001,2)) * 2^m_pos; m_pos increments by 1 when a position is closed at a loss, increments by 2 when closed profitably with >120 Point distance, resets to 0 when closed profitably with <=120 Point distance

custom_logic_notes: The close() function iterates OrdersTotal()-1 but uses m_position.SelectByIndex(cnt) which is designed for PositionsTotal(), not OrdersTotal. This is likely a bug - OrdersTotal() counts pending orders while SelectByIndex works with positions. The m_pos martingale counter has a complex update rule: +1 on closing a losing position (in closeAll), +2 on closing a profitable position with >120 Point move (in close()), and reset to 0 on closing a profitable position with <=120 Point move (in closeAll). The MACD value is multiplied by 1000000 which makes the threshold comparison with 230 meaningful - this scaling factor is symbol-dependent and may not work for all instruments. The buy() and sell() functions check m_buy_total==0 and m_sell_total==0 respectively, meaning only one position per side is allowed, but opposite side is closed first.
python_conversion_notes: The martingale lot sizing with m_pos state tracking across position closes requires careful state management in Python. The MACD*1000000 scaling is non-standard and must be replicated exactly. The close() function appears to have a bug using OrdersTotal() with position selection - in Python backtesting, decide whether to replicate the bug or fix it. No SL/TP means all exits are signal-based or the 120*Point profit-taking rule. The intrabar repeat-while-true behavior means signals are evaluated every tick, not just on new bars. The m_pos counter is the critical state variable - it persists across ticks and is updated only when positions are closed, affecting next trade size exponentially.
